summary.title: NVIDIA Vera CPU
summary.one_liner: NVIDIA's product page for Vera, an Arm-compatible data center CPU with 88 custom Olympus cores, LPDDR5X memory, and NVLink-C2C links, aimed at agentic AI and reinforcement learning workloads.
takeaways: Vera has 88 custom NVIDIA Olympus Arm cores, with Spatial Multithreading giving 176 threads with partitioned core resources.
It pairs LPDDR5X memory (up to 1.2 TB/s bandwidth, up to 1.5 TB capacity) with SOCAMM modules, and connects to Rubin GPUs over NVLink-C2C at up to 1.8 TB/s.
NVIDIA claims up to 80% faster agentic task completion and up to 1.8x over leading x86 CPUs on agent-loop workloads, based on its own measured data.
Vera is offered as a host CPU for Vera Rubin NVL72 and HGX Vera Rubin NVL8 systems, as standalone dual- and single-socket servers, or as a liquid-cooled rack.
The page links a whitepaper for the architecture but the page text itself gives no clock speeds, prices, or independent benchmark numbers.
summary.summary: This NVIDIA product page presents Vera as a CPU for agentic AI and reinforcement learning, covering tool use, code execution, sandboxing, and data processing. It lists architecture features: 88 Olympus cores, a single monolithic compute die connected by second-generation Scalable Coherency Fabric (3.4 TB/s bisectional bandwidth), LPDDR5X memory on SOCAMM modules, and NVLink-C2C coupling to GPUs. Performance claims (up to 80% faster agentic task completion, 1.8x over x86, 5x bandwidth per watt of memory power) are relative figures from NVIDIA's own measured and projected data. The page is mostly marketing and links to a whitepaper and deep-dive posts for architecture details; it gives no pricing or independent benchmarks.
